input.quote: Thereafter, this Agreement shall automatically renew for subsequent one (1) year periods unless either party provides the other party with written notification at least thirty (30) days prior to the expiration of the initial five (5) year term or any one (1) year renewal thereof of its intention to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 11.1 already meets the preferred structure on renewal length (one-year renewals) and exit (30 days' notice, exercisable by Corio). However, it omits two preferred elements: a Commerce One reminder 60 days before each renewal, and any cap on renewal pricing. Exhibit B pricing (p0153-p0154) only states "Year 2-5, and beyond: [*]" and Section 4 contains no uplift limit, so renewal-term fee increases are uncapped. The redline adds the 60-day renewal reminder and caps renewal increases at the lesser of CPI and 3%, with a 5% fallback offered in the comment.

proposal.summary: Add vendor renewal reminder (60 days) and cap renewal fee increases at lesser of CPI and 3%
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The one-year auto-renewal and 30-day non-renewal notice work for us, but we have added a 60-day advance renewal reminder from Commerce One and a cap on renewal fee increases at the lesser of CPI and 3%, consistent with our position that renewals be easy to exit and predictably priced. If a hard cap is an issue, we can accept a 5% ceiling.

ops.oldText: of its intention to terminate this Agreement.
ops.newText: of its intention to terminate this Agreement. Commerce One shall provide Corio with written notice of each upcoming renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the expiration of the then-current term. The fees payable for any renewal term shall not increase by more than the lesser of (i) the percentage increase in the U.S. Consumer Price Index (All Urban Consumers) over the preceding twelve (12) months and (ii) three percent (3%) of the fees payable for the immediately preceding term.
